2:
SAY:
- Read the cultural sensitivity statement aloud, in a calm voice.
- 'Today we are writing about the Coorong, which sits on Ngarrindjeri Country.'
- 'We acknowledge their custodianship of this land.'

DO:
- Pause briefly so students take it in.
- Move on without inviting discussion.

TEACHER NOTES:
Deliver as a one-minute orientation. Not a discussion task.

SENSITIVITY ADVISORY:
- What it is: references to deceased persons, historical perspectives, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander histories and cultures, including Ngarrindjeri Country.
- Framing language: see SAY.
- Watch for: students who may have personal or cultural connections; signs of discomfort.
- Protocol: pause if a student is distressed, offer a quiet seat or water, let the student step out and rejoin without comment.

WATCH FOR:
- Body language at the moment of reading.

[Stage: Lesson Orientation]
7:

- 'If writing a body paragraph feels new, that is okay. We will build it together.'

DO:
- Point to each SC.
- Tap the writing criterion twice so students hold it as today's writing focus.

TEACHER NOTES:
This lesson turns lesson 19's plan into prose. Editing is the closing skill - keep time for it.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who say they did not finish lesson 19's plan; pair them or use the modelled SPO.

21:
SAY:
- 'What happens during the Bonney Upwelling? Show me on your fingers.'
- 'One: South Australia and Victoria are impacted.'
- 'Two: it occurs from November to May.'
- 'Three: spring winds shift to the southeast and drive an ocean current northwest along the coast.'
- 'Four: it acts as national protection for endangered ecosystems.'
- Ask: 'Three, two, one, show.' Expected: 3.

DO:
- Scan boards.
- Ask: 'Why three?' Expected: 'because that is what the text says happens during the upwelling.'

CFU CHECKPOINT:
Technique: Show Fingers 1-4
Script:
- 'Show me what happens during the Bonney Upwelling.'
- Scan for: clear majority on 3.
PROCEED:
- Confirm 3 and re-read the text on slide 12.
PIVOT:
- Most likely misconception: students pick 2 (timing) instead of the action.
- Reteach with the rule: 'Two tells us when. Three tells us what happens. The question asks what.'
- Re-check: 'Show me again.'

WATCH FOR:
- Students who pick 1 (places) - those are where, not what.

[Stage: CFU | Comprehension]
22:
SAY:
- 'Now we move to writing. We will turn our SPO from lesson 19 into a full body paragraph.'

DO:
- Display and move on.

TEACHER NOTES:
Keep students with their SPOs in front of them.

[Stage: Text-Level Writing]
23:
SAY:
- 'Watch this first.'
- 'Information reports have these features. Listen for each one.'
- 'Most often written in present tense. Third person pronouns - it, they, the Coorong. Subheadings for emphasis. Simple and expanded noun groups. Adjectives and adverbials to build description. Technical language and precise vocabulary. Action verbs and relating verbs. May include images or labelled diagrams.'

DO:
- Read each feature.
- Tap on present tense and third person twice - common student errors.

TEACHER NOTES:
Display this list nearby for the writing block.

[Stage: I Do | Genre Features]
24:
SAY:
- 'Identify the technical or precise vocabulary in this extract.'
- 'It is home to both local birds and migratory species that travel from as far as Alaska and Siberia. An event known as the Bonney Upwelling occurs due to an influx of water from Antarctica that leaves behind nutrients that many species, particularly marine animals, rely on to survive.'
- Ask: 'Whiteboards: write three technical or precise words. Three minutes.'

DO:
- Circulate; read several boards.
- Reveal: migratory, species, Bonney Upwelling, influx, nutrients, marine.
- Cold call one student.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who pick simple words (it, the); redirect to technical or precise words.

[Stage: We Do | Vocabulary]
25:
SAY:
- 'Identify six adjectives in this extract.'
- 'The Coorong ecosystem is unique and complex, home to many vulnerable and endangered species. The large-scale removal of local wetland environments has reduced the number of plants and wildlife that depend on this area.'
- Ask: 'Whiteboards: list the six adjectives. Three minutes.'

DO:
- Circulate; read several boards.
- Reveal: unique, complex, vulnerable, endangered, large-scale, local.
- Ask: 'How does each adjective help the reader?'

WATCH FOR:
- Students who include nouns; remind them adjectives describe nouns.

[Stage: We Do | Adjectives]
26:
SAY:
- 'Identify words or phrases that show this extract is in the present tense.'
- 'The Coorong is a rich environment teeming with various local and migratory species unlike anywhere else in the world.'
- Ask: 'Whiteboards. Three, two, one, show.' Expected: is, teeming.

DO:
- Scan boards.
- Ask: 'How can we tell those words show present tense?'

WATCH FOR:
- Students who pick 'rich' or 'migratory' - those are descriptors, not tense markers.

[Stage: We Do | Tense]
27:
SAY:
- 'Eight words. Which are technical and precise and could be useful for our paragraph?'
- 'Words: favourite, disappointing, migratory, large-scale, nutrients, species, environment, like.'
- Ask: 'Whiteboards: write the technical and precise words. Three minutes.'

DO:
- Scan boards.
- Reveal: migratory, large-scale, nutrients, species, environment.
- Ask: 'Why not favourite or disappointing?' Expected: 'those are opinions, not facts.'

CFU CHECKPOINT:
Technique: Whiteboard Show + Cold Call
Script:
- 'Show me your technical words.'
- Scan for: 80% have at least three of the five correct words.
PROCEED:
- Move to turning the SPO into a paragraph.
PIVOT:
- Most likely misconception: students confuse opinion words with technical words.
- Reteach with the rule: 'Information reports use facts, not opinions. Favourite is an opinion.'
- Re-check: 'Show me again.'

WATCH FOR:
- Students who include 'like' - it is a vague filler word.

[Stage: CFU | Vocabulary]
28:
SAY:
- 'Today we are writing body paragraph three using our notes from lesson 19.'
- 'Our topic is the Coorong. The paragraph focus is flora and fauna.'
- 'Watch this first. I will model how to turn the SPO into full sentences.'

DO:
- Frame the writing task.
- Have students place their SPO from lesson 19 next to their booklet.

[Stage: I Do | Frame]
29:
SAY:
- 'Here is the SPO we built last lesson. Read it with me.'
- Choral read each part of the SPO.
- 'Notice the brevity in the SDs.'

DO:
- Choral read the SPO.
- Tap each part to anchor the structure.

TEACHER NOTES:
Students will use this as the source for today's writing.

[Stage: I Do | SPO Recap]
30:
SAY:
- 'First step. The TS is already written - we keep it as is.'
- 'TS: The Coorong ecosystem is unique and complex, home to many vulnerable and endangered species.'
- Ask: 'What is the main idea of this paragraph?' Expected: 'vulnerable and endangered species.'

DO:
- Read the TS aloud.
- Cold call one student.

TEACHER NOTES:
Quick recap of TS purpose before turning the SDs into sentences.

[Stage: I Do | TS]
31:
SAY:
- 'Watch this first. I am going to turn SD1 into a full sentence.'
- 'SD1 in note form: removal of wetland equals down arrow plants and wildlife leads-to reliant on area.'
- 'I convert the symbols into words. Equals becomes has. Down arrow becomes reduced. Leads-to becomes that depend on.'
- 'I add technical terms: large-scale, environments, area.'
- 'My full sentence: The large-scale removal of local wetland environments has reduced the number of plants and wildlife that depend on this area.'

DO:
- Highlight each symbol as you convert it.
- Show the new technical words appearing in colour if your set-up allows.

TEACHER NOTES:
This is the core skill of the lesson.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who think they can keep symbols in the final paragraph; symbols are for planning only.

[Stage: I Do | Convert SD1]
32:
SAY:
- 'Now we expand SD1 fully and add details. Watch this first.'
- 'I need to check that my sentence is in present tense, third person, with technical vocabulary.'
- 'My sentence: The large-scale removal of local wetland environments has reduced the number of plants and wildlife that depend on this area.'
- 'Notice the highlighted words - those are added to make a complete sentence with clarifying details.'

DO:
- Highlight the added words on screen.
- Read the sentence aloud as one piece.

TEACHER NOTES:
The colour coding shows what was added; planning notes do not include all words.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who copy the SPO note as the sentence.

[Stage: I Do | Expand SD1]
33:
SAY:
- 'We do one together. Read SD1 again as a full sentence.'
- 'The large-scale removal of local wetland environments has reduced the number of plants and wildlife that depend on this area.'
- 'Now your turn. SD2 in note form: home leads-to birds and migratory species leads-to Alaska and Siberia.'
- Ask: 'On your whiteboards, write SD2 as a full sentence. Three minutes.'

DO:
- Time the work.
- Circulate; read several boards.
- Cold call one student to share theirs.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who keep arrows in the sentence; symbols are only for the plan.

[Stage: We Do | Convert SD2]
34:
SAY:
- 'Reveal time. Here is the SD2 sentence: It is home to both local birds and migratory species that travel from as far as Alaska and Siberia.'
- Ask: 'Compare with your version. What did the model add? What is similar to yours?'

DO:
- Reveal sentence.
- Cold call two students to compare.
- Highlight added details: 'both local birds', 'travel', 'as far as'.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who deflate when their sentence is shorter; reassure them their version still works as long as it has the SD facts.

[Stage: We Do | Compare]
35:
SAY:
- 'Now SD3. Read the note: Bonney Upwelling leads-to up arrow water leads-to Antarctica leads-to leaves nutrients leads-to marine animals equals require for survival.'
- Ask: 'On your whiteboards, write SD3 as a full sentence. Three minutes.'
- 'Then we add the CS that summarises the paragraph.'

DO:
- Time the work.
- Circulate; read several boards.
- Reveal: 'An event known as the Bonney Upwelling occurs due to an influx of water from Antarctica that leaves behind nutrients that many species, particularly marine animals, rely on to survive.'
- Show the CS: 'The Coorong is a rich environment teeming with various local and migratory species unlike anywhere else in the world.'
- Ask: 'What word in the CS echoes the TS?' Expected: species, environment.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who write a long SD3 with too many ideas; one fact per SD.

[Stage: We Do | Convert SD3]
36:
SAY:
- 'Three sentences expand the same SD. Which is most effective?'
- 'SD: Coorong equals home leads-to mammal, reptile species and plant species.'
- 'Sentence one: The Coorong contains a wide array of flora and fauna.'
- 'Sentence two: The Coorong contains various endangered extinct species who are being threatened due to lack of water flow.'
- 'Sentence three: The Coorong ecosystem supports life of over 40 mammal and reptile species as well as 278 plant species.'
- Ask: 'Whiteboards: write 1, 2 or 3. Then talk to your partner about why.'

DO:
- Time partner talk for 90 seconds.
- Cold call two pairs to share.
- Confirm: sentence three. One is too vague. Two introduces a new idea. Three expands with precise numbers.

CFU CHECKPOINT:
Technique: Whiteboard Show + Partner Talk
Script:
- 'Show me which sentence is most effective.'
- Scan for: clear majority on 3.
PROCEED:
- Confirm 3 and review why.
PIVOT:
- Most likely misconception: students pick sentence one because it sounds neat.
- Reteach with the rule: 'A wide array does not give numbers or specifics. SDs need facts.'
- Re-check: 'Show me again.'

WATCH FOR:
- Students who pick sentence two because it sounds dramatic.

[Stage: CFU | Expand]
37:
SAY:
- 'Read the completed paragraph chorally with me.'
- Choral read the full paragraph.
- 'Notice the present tense, the third person, and the technical vocabulary.'
- Ask: 'Which features of an information report can you spot?'

DO:
- Choral read.
- Cold call one student.

TEACHER NOTES:
Display this during the writing block.

[Stage: We Do | Read Final]
38:
SAY:
- 'Open your booklet to Lesson 20 - Write a body paragraph for an information report.'
- 'Step one: copy or refine your TS.'
- 'Step two: turn each SD into a full sentence.'
- 'Step three: write a CS that echoes the TS.'
- 'Use present tense, third person, and technical vocabulary.'

DO:
- Set timer.
- Distribute booklets if needed.
- Circulate; check the TS first.
- Pull a small group for re-modelling.

ENABLING & EXTENDING:
ENABLING PROMPT:
- Task: provide the modelled TS and CS; students just write the three SDs as full sentences.
- Extra Notes: pair with a peer.
EXTENDING PROMPT:
- Task: write a second body paragraph on a different topic from the non-fiction text. Use the same structure.

TEACHER NOTES:
The booklet is the You Do for the writing objective.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who keep symbols in their paragraph.
- Students who slip into past tense; redirect to present.
- Students who use opinion words.

[Stage: You Do | Booklet]
39:
SAY:
- 'After writing, re-read your paragraph. Use the checklist in your booklet to edit.'
- 'Check that your TS clearly expresses the main idea.'
- 'Check your SDs expand on the TS.'
- 'Check you have used adjectives, technical vocabulary, present tense.'
- 'Check your CS summarises without repeating.'
- 'Check spelling, punctuation and grammar.'
- 'Edit in a different colour if you can.'

DO:
- Set a 10-minute editing window.
- Circulate. Read 1 to 2 students' paragraphs and discuss specific edits.
- Pull a small group for students who edited nothing.

TEACHER NOTES:
Editing is part of the lesson goal. Do not let it slip - 10 minutes minimum.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who change nothing; cold call them with one specific edit suggestion.
- Students who delete most of their work; redirect to surface edits first.

[Stage: You Do | Edit]
